One hundred and thirty-nine works. The last twelve trace scores read 2, 2, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 1 — median 2, ceiling unmoved. The two scores of 1 in that window came from the luggage-wall piece and the plantation-tourism piece; in both cases the formal accident was present but absorbed too quietly into a resolved composition to change what the image was arguing. The trace-3 and trace-4 moments in the archive — the salmon-pink dress, the sandals at Djibouti, the mop smear, the bent beam — all share a single quality absent from the recent run: the accident didn't decorate the frame, it reassigned the subject. Nothing in the last twelve did that.

Camera position has not moved. Straight-on leads at 27, overhead at 16, from-behind at 14, and the recent window added nothing outside that band. A low-angle optically generated scale rupture — where lens position rather than object size creates the perceptual break — has appeared six times across 139 works and zero times in the last twelve. That is still the clearest unoccupied formal territory in the archive.

Figure dynamics remain the archive's most persistent unresolved problem. Two or more figures appeared once in the last twelve; a second figure actively contradicting or reframing the first has not occurred in 139 works. They flank, they parallel, they echo. The collision that would make two figures more dangerous than one has not been attempted.

Register distribution: aftermath and menace are tied at 26 each, suspension at 18, endurance at 13, defiance now at 12. Reckoning last appeared in July. Reprieve appeared once. Absurdity surfaced twice and was set down. These are not exhausted registers — they were demonstrated as workable and remain available — but returning to any of them is only worth doing if the anchor produces a formal problem that register hasn't yet solved.

Title grammar has narrowed to Wh- clauses and the miscellaneous other category. No new grammar form has entered in over two months. The paired-noun-comma form appeared three times in the recent window but remains underused across the full archive relative to how much structural work it can do.

One hundred and thirty-nine works have achieved coherence. The current risk is not incoherence but a settled fluency that stops just short of rupture every time.
